name: UN Women
body: Every page analyzed has a meta description, every image has alt text, and HSTS is preloaded. But /en sends over 700 KB of HTML before any image or script, and all 17 pages analyzed weigh more than 500 KB.
lesson: Move what inflates the HTML, like inline data or repeated menus, into cached files.
summary: www.unwomen.org scores 78 out of 100 (C). 3 checks fail now, 20 are at risk, and 22 pass. Fix first: 14 form controls have no label.

fix.title: 14 form controls have no label
fix.evidence: On /en/about-us, /en/about-us/about-un-women, /en/about-us/guiding-documents, /en/where-we-are and 10 more. Screen readers announce them as an unnamed field.
fix.fix: Pair each control with <label for>, wrap it in a label, or add aria-label.

fix.title: No content security policy
fix.evidence: content-security-policy was absent on the start page. Missing on all 17 pages analyzed. Injected scripts are not limited by the browser.
fix.fix: Start with the Report-Only policy in the fix kit, watch the reports for a week, then enforce it.

fix.title: Referrer-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Browsers fall back to their default. An explicit policy keeps full URLs from leaking to other sites. Missing on all 17 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Permissions-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Embedded content can ask for the camera, microphone, or location. Missing on all 17 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Tracking tags load with no consent tool in the page
fix.evidence: Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, Google Ads appear in the HTML and no consent platform or Google Consent Mode default was found. In the EU, the UK, Brazil, and Colombia this is a legal exposure.
fix.fix: Add a consent platform and set Google Consent Mode v2 defaults to denied before any tag loads.

fix.title: Core Web Vitals fail for real visitors
fix.evidence: Real Chrome users over the last 28 days on this page, at the 75th percentile: Largest Contentful Paint 2.4 s (good), Interaction to Next Paint 2008 ms (poor), Cumulative Layout Shift 0.01 (good). Source: Chrome UX Report through PageSpeed Insights.
fix.fix: Break up long JavaScript tasks behind clicks and taps, and defer third-party scripts.
